name: Delhivery
summary: Delhivery is an Indian logistics company offering express parcel delivery, part and full truckload freight, warehousing and supply chain services to businesses. Candidates commonly report problem-solving and design rounds for technology roles, and case-style or operational questions for supply chain, operations and business roles, often about networks, hubs and on-time delivery.
rounds: Online test or coding round for technology roles (often)
Technical rounds on problem-solving, data and your projects
Case or operations round for supply chain, analytics and business roles
looks_for: Operational thinking: hubs, routes, capacity and turnaround time
Comfort with large, messy data from real-world operations
Ownership on the ground: fixing problems at a facility or on a route
Care for both the business shipping a parcel and the person receiving it
Safety and process discipline in warehouses and on the road

questions.text: Tell me about a time you improved how something worked on the ground, not just on paper.
covers: What you saw first-hand that the reports missed
The change you made with the people doing the work
The result: time, errors or cost, with a number if possible

questions.text: Describe a time you had to deal with an operational crisis, such as a sudden backlog or breakdown.
covers: What happened and how big the impact was
How you set priorities and who you brought in
How you cleared it and what you changed to prevent a repeat

questions.text: Tell me about a time you used data to convince people who were sceptical.
covers: What they believed and why
The data you gathered and how you presented it simply
Whether they changed their minds, and what happened next

questions.text: Tell me about a time you managed a team or vendor who wasn't meeting expectations.
covers: The gap, stated with facts
The conversation you had and the support or deadline you set
The outcome, including if you had to escalate or replace them

questions.text: How would you design a system that tracks a parcel from pickup to delivery and shows customers an accurate status?
covers: Scan events at each step flowing into an event stream
Handling late, missing or out-of-order scans without confusing the customer
Serving status and an estimated delivery time at scale

questions.text: Deliveries from one hub have been running late all week. How would you find the cause?
covers: Locating the delay: inbound, sorting, line haul or last mile
Comparing with other hubs and with the same hub last month
Likely causes (volume, staffing, vehicles, a process change) and a quick test of each

questions.text: How would you plan delivery routes for riders in a busy part of Mumbai each morning?
covers: Inputs: addresses, time windows, parcel sizes, rider capacity
A practical approach: cluster by area, then order stops; exact solutions don't scale
Adjusting for traffic and failed attempts during the day

questions.text: Festive season volumes are coming. How would you prepare a sorting centre for the peak?
covers: Forecasting volume by day and planning staff, shifts and vehicles
Space, equipment checks and training temporary staff early
Daily tracking during the peak and a plan if volume exceeds the forecast

questions.text: Many deliveries fail because the customer isn't home. What would you try to reduce failed attempts?
covers: Measuring where and when failures happen most
Ideas: confirming slots, live tracking links, calling ahead, pickup points
Testing one idea in a few areas and measuring the cost against the gain

questions.text: How would you predict a sensible delivery date to show a buyer at checkout?
covers: Inputs: pickup and drop pin codes, route history, cut-off times, current load
A simple model first, then improving it with data
Balancing a promise that's attractive with one that's reliable

questions.text: Explain the difference between express parcel delivery and part truckload freight, and how their operations differ.
covers: Express parcel: many small shipments, often to homes, speed matters
Part truckload: larger business loads that share a truck between customers
How sorting, vehicles and pricing differ between the two

questions.text: How would you decide where to place a new warehouse for a brand that sells across India?
covers: Where the demand is, and the delivery speed the brand wants to offer
Transport costs, land and labour availability
Comparing a few options with rough numbers, and the trade-off you'd accept
What interests you about moving goods at scale
Something specific about Delhivery's services or network
The kind of problem you'd like to own

questions.text: Are you comfortable working at a hub or warehouse, including shifts, if the role needs it?
covers: An honest answer about shifts and location
Any time you've worked in an operational setting
Why being close to the work would help you

tips: Learn the vocabulary: first mile, middle mile, last mile, hub, sort centre, line haul, RTO (return to origin), turnaround time.
In cases, follow the parcel from pickup to sorting, line haul and last mile, and find where the delay or cost sits.
Mention seasonality: festive sales and shopping events change volumes sharply.
For tech roles, show you understand messy real-world data: missed scans, wrong addresses, late updates.
